amendments.pair_caveat: Generation pairs also change size, and within the Qwen3 line the item share runs 0.49 / 0.89 / 0.70 / 0.71 across 4B / 8B / 14B / 32B (original environment, transformers 4.51.3), so a 'differs' here is not a generation effect: it describes two whole models.
amendments.serve2_rescoring: Amended 2026-11-23, after the environment check failed and its cause was found, before any wave B score existed (design section 8; corrected after review 2, 2026-11-24). The check stays FAILED: Qwen3-8B's yes/no per-score difference was 0.248 nats, about seven times the archived cross-GPU difference (0.035), and Mistral 7B passed narrowly (0.069 against 0.07). A float64 diagnostic showed that the float64 logits themselves changed between the environments (median relative change 0.44%, about the bf16 unit roundoff 2^-8 of the logit, which at these logits is about one bf16 step), so the hidden state differs (inferred, not measured); Qwen's large readout logits make that about a quarter of a nat; bf16 rounding is not the cause. This amendment replaces the gate; it does not satisfy it. Every older model used in a wave B comparison is rescored in serve2 on every item and condition (RESCORE_MODELS), and every comparison, planned or descriptive, uses those rescorings. Wave B is read only when every rescoring passes rescore_check (complete and covering every scored item with matching item hashes; token ids identical between the study stack and serve2, compared at the rescoring's commit; its pinned GPU type; its gate and loading check passed in transformers 5 at the pinned revision; for node-local weights, its files matched the manifest) and the analysis's references read exactly those rescorings. The label 'not interpretable (environment check)' now means that the serve2 rescorings have not passed. The original-environment scores are reported beside the serve2 ones, descriptively; a reference whose item share moves by more than 0.02 or whose yes/no goal effect moves by more than 0.10 nats between the environments is 'environment-dependent', and every comparison involving it is reported with both readings (the serve2 reading stands). The six item-share tests, the 16-test Holm family, the thresholds and the competence gate are unchanged.

formats: Amended 2026-11-20, before any wave A score was read: the yes/no format is the primary cross-family comparison, read through the item share moved toward Yes (third amendment: the single primary metric, per model and in the planned paired comparisons, one Holm-corrected family; a model must pass the competence gate); the goal-to-evidence ratio R, ΔL and the standardised d are secondary, and the two-candidate format is read within model only. Across families R mostly reflects how far each model pushes its log-odds on failures, not goal bias. The two-candidate score's validity was checked for Qwen3 only; Llama-3.1-8B's sign of L agreed with its written predictions on 65% of pilot items (notes/deviations.md). The logged prediction is unchanged.

prediction: Logged before any wave B score (2026-11-22). B1: the goal effect (aligned minus swapped) is positive in both formats (95% game-clustered CI above zero) for every wave B run, and the item share is supported for every wave B model that passes the competence gate. B2: no generation pair reads 'differs' with the newer model lower. B3: in the plain format, instruct minus base reads 'differs' (or 'differs, within the margin') with a positive difference; untestable if the base model fails the competence gate. Amended after review 1, before any wave B score (notes/families_waveb_review1.md): B1's basis holds for the log-odds effect (every interpretable model scored so far has it), not for the item share: Qwen3-4B is competent yet its share is 0.49 with a yes/no effect of 2.27 nats, so a share that is not supported while the yes/no effect's CI is above zero reads 'effect carried by a minority of items (as Qwen3-4B)', and 'no detectable effect' only when both are null. B2 can fail only on a clear negative difference ('inconclusive' and 'matches' count as holding). B3: if the base model fails only the yes/no coverage criterion, B3 is read on the two-candidate item share (B3_FALLBACK).
